facts.text: Rockford Bay sits on land that was home to the Schitsu'umsh people of the Coeur d'Alene Tribe for millennia before European settlers arrived.
Rockford Bay lies 12.5 miles south-southwest of the city of Coeur d'Alene, perched on the lake’s western shore.
Between East Point and Rockford Point, the bay’s depths range from 15 to 19 meters, nurturing beds of Potamogeton aquatic plants.
A joint Idaho Department of Fish and Game–Kootenai County site offers a boat ramp, dock, and parking for fishing and boating enthusiasts.
Rockford Bay receives about 25 inches of rain yearly, with November averaging 3.8 inches and August dropping to just 0.9 inches.
The lake basin that surrounds Rockford Bay was carved by Pleistocene outburst floods from glacial Lake Missoula, leaving thick gravel layers.
